claims.statement: No EXIF or XMP metadata present
claims.limitations: Absence does NOT indicate authenticity or manipulation: WhatsApp, Instagram, X, Facebook and most platforms strip metadata on upload, and generators often write none.
claims.what_would_confirm: Obtain the earliest available copy (ideally the uploader's original file).
claims.why: The file carries no camera or editing metadata.

claims.statement: JPEG encoded at approx. quality 55 with standard libjpeg-style quantisation tables
claims.limitations: Recompression replaces the tables, so this reflects the last encoder only.
claims.why: Quantisation tables are read directly from the JPEG header. Custom tables identify encoder families (camera firmware, Photoshop, platform re-encoders).

claims.statement: No C2PA / Content Credentials manifest found
claims.limitations: Absence does NOT indicate authenticity: most media has no C2PA, and platforms strip manifests on re-upload. Many generators do not sign their output.
claims.what_would_confirm: Check earlier copies — the earliest discovered copy is the most likely to retain a manifest.
claims.why: The file carries no embedded provenance manifest.

claims.statement: No open (DWT-DCT) Stable Diffusion watermark recovered
claims.limitations: Absence does not indicate authenticity: the watermark is optional, fragile to resizing/recompression, and most generators use other or no watermarks.

claims.statement: No generator metadata or declared AI source type found
claims.limitations: Absence does NOT indicate a camera origin: platforms strip metadata and most generators can be configured to write none.

claims.statement: ELA: localised regions recompress very differently from the rest of the image (p99/median block ratio 25.9)
claims.limitations: ELA is noisy: high-contrast edges, text, smooth skies and recompression all change error levels. Useful for directing attention, not as standalone evidence. Uniform ELA does not show authenticity (fully generated images are often uniform).
claims.why: Regions pasted or regenerated after the last JPEG save often show a different error level.

claims.statement: Sensor-noise residual is inconsistent across regions (block coefficient of variation 1.41)
claims.limitations: Texture, exposure, denoising and blur all change local noise. Requires visual review of the map; does not identify a generator.
claims.why: Camera images carry roughly uniform sensor noise; spliced or regenerated regions often differ.

claims.statement: Frequency spectrum shows no strong periodic peaks (peak score 2.7)
claims.limitations: Resizing, JPEG 8×8 blocking, screen capture moiré and halftone patterns also create peaks. Modern diffusion models often leave none.
claims.why: Transposed-convolution / upsampling in many GANs and some diffusion decoders leaves grid-like spectral peaks.

claims.limitations: Small, profile or occluded faces may be missed.

claims.statement: Burned-in text read from the media (1 line(s)): @leaky_news EXCLUSIVE
claims.limitations: OCR can misread stylised fonts; verify against the image.
claims.why: Text overlays (captions, watermarks) were read directly from the pixels.

claims.statement: Handle “@leaky_news” is visible in the media
claims.limitations: A visible handle shows that the name was overlaid at some stage — it may belong to an earlier uploader, a reposter, or be deliberately misleading. It does not show who made the content.
claims.what_would_confirm: Locate the account and capture its public post of this media.
claims.why: Platforms (e.g. TikTok, Reels) burn the uploader's handle into downloaded videos; reposters also add their own handles.

claims.statement: Camera-processing fingerprints: Flat areas are very smooth and show no brightness-dependent noise: consistent with strong denoising, heavy compression or an image that never had sensor noise.
claims.limitations: Does not distinguish denoising from synthetic origin or from low-ISO capture of a smooth scene.
claims.what_would_confirm: Independent confirmation with a validated method, reference material, or the original file.

claims.statement: Camera-processing fingerprints: None of the four camera-processing traces could be found. This is what resized, re-encoded, screenshotted, rendered or generated pixels look like — and also what a social-media copy of a real photo looks like.
claims.limitations: This does NOT mean the image is fake. Treat it as: origin cannot be supported from the pixels.
claims.what_would_confirm: Independent confirmation with a validated method, reference material, or the original file.

claims.statement: Editing and recompression analysis: 1 pair(s) of image regions share matching local features with a consistent geometric transform (strongest: 15 matches, scale 0.997×).
claims.limitations: Repeating patterns (windows, tiles, foliage, text, crowds) and symmetric objects match too. Review the two regions by eye. In validation this flag fired on 0% of 160 real web photographs (95 % interval 0%–2%).
claims.what_would_confirm: Independent confirmation with a validated method, reference material, or the original file.
claims.why: Duplicating part of a picture to hide or add something creates two regions with identical local structure.

claims.statement: Editing and recompression analysis: 1 region(s) show at least two independent cues at once (largest: 12 tiles; cues: JPEG grid, copy-move).
claims.limitations: A lead for human review only. Screenshots, overlaid text/stickers and platform processing can also stack cues. Not a conclusion that anything was altered. In validation this flag fired on 6% of 160 real web photographs (95 % interval 3%–11%).
claims.what_would_confirm: Independent confirmation with a validated method, reference material, or the original file.
claims.why: Independent measurements (compression level, demosaicing, JPEG grid, resampling, duplication) rarely misfire at the same spot.

claims.statement: A copy of the same underlying media (“Forum [DEMO]: anon_uploader_77”) carries verified generation evidence: Embedded generation parameters identify the tool family: Stable Diffusion (AUTOMATIC1111/Forge-style parameters); model/checkpoint: sd_xl_base_1.0
claims.limitations: Rests on two links: the match (shared content) and the provenance claim on the other copy. Generator metadata can in principle be added to an image deliberately.
claims.why: This file was matched to that copy through geometrically verified links, and that copy carries generator provenance. Provenance metadata is usually stripped when media is re-shared, so it survives on few copies.

verdict.headline: Fake
reasons: Proof in the file: A copy of the same underlying media (“Forum [DEMO]: anon_uploader_77”) carries verified generation evidence: Embedded generation parameters identify the tool family: Stable Diffusion (AUTOMATIC1111/Forge-style parameters); model/checkpoint: sd_xl_base_1.0.
caveats: A verdict says how the picture was made, not who made it or whether the event it shows happened.
verdict.reliability: Tested on 640 images from AI generators and photo sources it had never seen: right 68% of the time overall — real photos called real 87%, fakes caught 48%; when the verdict is not 'Uncertain' it was right 74%.
verdict.summary: This is very likely fake (AI-generated image) — 99% likely fake.
